doc.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024

chapter: Les Brown, Bob Hope and Vietnam
title: Big bands of the late 1960s and early 70s; Ted Lewis recalled
summary: Hal lists road bands he worked with: Ray Anthony, Freddy Martin, Harry James and Billy Vaughan; Ted Lewis is named.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Right. Yeah that was in 60- — I started in 1969 until Bob Hope’s last trip which was in ’72. He did ’69, ’70, ’71 and ’72. And you know the big band era, it started to fold I guess when Tommy Dorsey died. I did get a chance to work with Bob Crosby but he wasn’t a big band then, but he was an old guy, an old band. But the bands were still working pretty well. Les Brown was working well, the road bands — you had road bands out there like Ray Anthony. And you know Ray Anthony is still alive. He’s 102, and I used to work with him all the time. And I worked with Freddy Martin, another old time band leader. And he worked quite a bit. He did cruises along with Ray Anthony doing cruises. Harry James, he was alive then still touring. I worked with Harry. I went down to South America with him, and Billy Vaughan. You may have not have heard of him because he’s not big in the U.S. He was big in Japan and South America. I took trips with him to Japan and to South America.
I thought of the guy who you were trying to mention, I think was it Ted Lewis?

Ted Lewis. He’s the guy that had the hat on. He was the other name, entertainer, that I played when I was 17. It was like wow. And then Marie McDonald was another one. She was an actress back in the ‘50s and ‘60s.
